items.title: 18 injured in suspected arson at Mississauga apartment building
items.summary: Residents in a Mississauga apartment building are shaken after a fire Monday morning, which police say may have been arson, sent at least 18 people to the hospital, including a firefighter and a police officer.

items.title: E-scooter ‘crisis’ prompts Mississauga to push for more regulations in Ontario
items.summary: Mississauga officials have stepped up efforts to get the provincial government to further regulate the use of e-scooters, with one city councillor saying the motorized micromobility devices have created a “crisis” situation where public safety is concerned. Mayor Carolyn Parrish said among other measures, she believes Ontario Transportation Minister Prabmeet Sarkaria may soon announce that police forces across the province will be further empowered to enforce rules of the road as they relate to e-scooters. ” The provincial government is expected to soon address the issue of e-scooters and e-bikes, with additional regulations anticipated sometime in the fall. Both Parrish and Ward 3 Coun. Chris Fonseca were part of a Mississauga delegation that attended the annual Association of Municipalities of Ontario conference last month in Ottawa, where e-scooter safety and additional regulations for the devices was among a number of issues city officials pushed the Ontario government on. Immediately after the conference, the city sent followup letters to the province laying out their concerns and wishes on mulitiple fronts. Ward 3 Coun. ” Speaking at last Wednesday’s city council meeting, Parrish described the trip to Ottawa as “really productive,” adding provincial ministers and other representatives the city met with “listened to us on several fronts,” including on the matter of e-scooter safety.

items.title: Peel police union endorses Alvin Tedjo for mayor of Mississauga
items.summary: The union representing nearly 4,000 uniformed and civilian members of the Peel Regional Police has endorsed Alvin Tedjo to be Mississauga’s next mayor. Peel Regional Police Association (PRPA) made the endorsement on Monday morning, opting to support the longtime Ward 2 councillor over other candidates that include incumbent Carolyn Parrish, former Mississauga mayor Bonnie Crombie, and current city councillor Dipika Dimerla. ” President Adrian Wooley said PRPA made the decision to lend its support for Tedjo, who represents the Clarkson and Lorne Park neighbourhoods, specifically because of his crime and safety plan. ” “We have worked alongside both Carolyn Parrish and Bonnie Crombie during their time leading the city, and we have not always felt the concerns of frontline officers or the public safety challenges facing Mississauga received the attention they deserved,” Wooley wrote. “Alvin has demonstrated a willingness to listen, work collaboratively with our officers and make public safety a priority.

items.title: 3-day Indigenous gathering, exhibit returns to Mississauga
items.summary: A three-day gathering and art exhibit returns to Mississauga this weekend. The sixth annual Gathering and Healing Weekend and Art Mashkiki Indigenous Art Exhibit is at the Small Arms Inspection Building in Mississauga Sept. 25 to 27, organizer Eagle Spirits of the Great Waters said. The free, public events offer opportunities for people of all ages to experience and learn about First Nations, Métis and Inuit arts and cultures through dance, music, storytelling, art, an Indigenous market, food and ceremony, the organization said. Eagle Spirits of the Great Waters is a Mississauga-based, Indigenous-led registered non-profit dedicated to celebrating and sharing Indigenous arts and cultures with all people. The annual Gathering and Healing Weekend is held in connection with National Truth and Reconciliation Day and creates an opportunity for Indigenous and non-Indigenous people to come together through culture, art, learning, remembrance and healing. The National Day for Truth and Reconciliation and Orange Shirt Day are both observed annually on Sept. 30, and they are dedicated to honouring Residential School Survivors, their families, and communities, and to recognize the lasting impacts of Canada’s Residential School system. The weekend event in Mississauga begins with an opening night reception on Friday, Sept. m. m. Opening night includes artists and Indigenous vendors, light refreshments, welcoming remarks, Eagle Spirits drumming, and live music by Dwayne Laforme and the Boogie Blues Band.

items.title: Mississauga firefighters raise alarm on staffing shortage — city says public safety not at risk
items.summary: City acknowledges staffing pressures, but says emergency response coverage has been maintained. The union representing firefighters says staffing shortages are impacting service. The union representing Mississauga firefighters is raising public alarm over daily staffing shortages and emergency vehicle reductions in the city. The Mississauga Fire Fighters Association (IAFF Local 1212) has posted several public statements on Facebook since August, stating that fire trucks are frequently taken out of service due to Mississauga Fire and Emergency Services (MFES) staffing shortages. The union first posted about six fire trucks being out of service on Aug. 22, across Wards 3, 5, 7 and 9, representing what it said was a drop in public protection, according to the social media post. Since then, the union has been sharing updates regularly about fire trucks taken out of service, with the last post on Sept. 17 noting that three trucks were out of service. “20 years ago, Mississauga had 30 front line fire trucks. Since then, nearly 100,000 more people, more highrises, more traffic and more emergencies. Today, we have 33 and three are out of service due to staffing shortages. This isn’t progress, it’s reduced protection. Mississauga, is this safe? Mississauga residents deserve to know when front line emergency response capacity is being reduced,” said the Sept.

items.title: Peel Regional Police report shows hate crimes increased by 17% in 2025
items.summary: Mississauga’s three divisions accounted for nearly 70 per cent of incidents. Peel Police release 2025 Annual Hate-Motivated Crime Report. Three Mississauga-based Peel Regional Police divisions reported nearly 70 per cent of hate crimes, according to the 2025 Annual Hate-Motivated Crime Report from June 2026. Of the 195 hate crimes recorded from January to December 2025 in Brampton and Mississauga, 136 were reported at the three Mississauga divisions. The report shows hate-motivated crimes in the two cities increased 17 per cent to 195 in 2025 from 166 in 2024. The report comes a year after Peel Regional Police transitioned investigative responsibility for hate-motivated crimes to its Hate Crime Unit in July 2025. Race, ethnicity and nationality were the most common motivating factors cited in 146 of the 195 incidents reported, an increase from 98 incidents reported in 2024. According to the report: In Peel, more than 69 per cent of residents are visible minorities from South Asian, Black, Asian (Chinese), Filipino and Arab ethnocultural backgrounds, according to the 2021 census.

items.title: Major road gets more dangerous driving complaints than any other in Mississauga
items.summary: Careless driving and speeding continue to top the list of complaints submitted to police through the Road Watch initiative in Mississauga, statistics to be presented to city officials this week show. Road Watch, a community-driven program that encourages people to report dangerous and aggressive drivers to police, recently released statistics that show 476 reports were received by Peel Regional Police from Jan. 1 through July 31, 2026 in Mississauga. Those numbers, which also show more cases of potentially dangerous driving behaviour were witnessed on Burnhamthorpe Road than any other road in the city, will be presented to the City of Mississauga’s Road Safety Committee on Tuesday morning. Road Watch statistics show 20 of the complaints were for incidents spotted on Burnhamthorpe Road, which is one of the city’s longest streets and crosses Mississauga from its western boundary to its eastern border with Toronto. Mississauga Road and Winston Churchill Boulevard were next on the list (see below), with 17 incidents reported on each of those arteries, while Dixie Road followed with 16 incidents called in to police. items.title: How the Peel police union is shaking up Mississauga’s mayoral race
items.summary: The Peel police union has snubbed front-runners Carolyn Parrish and Bonnie Crombie to endorse Alvin Tedjo for mayor. Mississauga mayoral hopeful Alvin Tedjo was endorsed by the Peel Regional Police Association in Mississauga on Monday, over the two front-runners in the race. The Peel police union has snubbed the two front-runners in the race for Mississauga mayor to endorse a third candidate, adding further intrigue to an election where safety, crime and the cost of policing are top issues. Alvin Tedjo’s plan to hire more officers was a key factor in the decision, said Adrian Woolley, president of the Peel Regional Police Association in an interview. “He’s young, he’s energetic, and he has ideas that are going to help the city,” said Woolley, noting it’s the first time the union has made an endorsement in a mayoral race; they endorsed a local Conservative MP candidate and Conservative government in the 2025 federal election. “A collaborative working relationship … is absolutely key and that’s certainly not what we have in the other two,” added Woolley. 5 million people. 3 million. 3 million.

items.title: Yom Kippur Prompts Extra Peel Police Patrols at Mississauga, Brampton Synagogues After Belleville Shooting
items.summary: Peel police say they have stepped up patrols around places of worship and cultural centres in Mississauga and Brampton after a shooting outside a synagogue in Belleville on Sunday night. According to police in Belleville, an officer came across an individual near Bleecker Avenue and Victoria Avenue, a mostly residential part of the city located about 180 kilometres east of Toronto, and an altercation left both the officer and the individual injured and taken to hospital. The incident happened near the Sons of Jacob Synagogue during a gathering to mark Yom Kippur. Ontario's Special Investigations Unit, which is automatically called in whenever a police interaction with the public results in serious injury, has been notified and is now involved. Belleville police say they are not providing further comment while that investigation proceeds. Peel police added that through the High Holidays period, including Yom Kippur, they have increased their presence around synagogues and cultural centres across Mississauga and Brampton as a precaution.

items.title: Rescue Effort at Burning Mississauga Apartment Leaves Officer and Firefighter Injured
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say an officer and a firefighter were both hurt early Monday morning while helping residents escape a fire at an apartment building near Inverhouse Drive and Lakeshore Road West. According to police, crews responded to the blaze, which broke out in a hallway, and found several people trapped inside suffering from smoke inhalation. Acting Sgt. Amanda Steenson told reporters that one of the officers was hurt while helping a firefighter pull a resident from the building during the rescue. Ten people were taken to hospital by ambulance as a result of the fire. The cause has not yet been determined, and police say an investigation into what sparked the blaze is underway. Steenson said investigators could release suspect information later if the fire is found to have been deliberately set.

If there’s ever a time to stop and appreciate the trees around us, it’s on September 23, National Tree Day. This day recognizes the important role trees play in our lives and in helping cities adapt to climate change. National Tree Day is part of National Forest Week. It’s a reminder that trees and our urban forests are an important part of a city. Trees help clean the air, support biodiversity and create greener and healthier cities. Trees can be seen as nature’s air conditioners. 4 degrees. As extreme weather becomes more common, a strong network of trees can keep neighbourhoods and buildings cool. Volunteers continue to ‘leaf’ their mark across Mississauga, planting trees and supporting environmental stewardship activities that help expand the city’s urban forest and green spaces. The City is continuing to advance its goal of One Million Trees by 2032, with 653,729 trees planted to date. Trees are planted across the city in various urban and green spaces.
